clue.text: Targets that could be a mistake

indicators.note: the phrase says these letters could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone warns that choosing these targets might be an error of judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To target something is to aim at it, so a phrase meaning lines up a shot fits the verb.

clue.text: Suppose idiot must go to university, supported by yours truly

indicators.note: the first piece has to travel on to join the next one in line
in a down clue the last piece sits underneath, holding up what comes before

parts.note: an ass is a fool
yours truly is the setter speaking of themself, so me

explanation.surface: A fool heading off to college, propped up by the speaker: an odd domestic arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something is to take it as true without proof, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Appearing upright before getting caught

parts.note: ere is the poetic word for before
Ct is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught (catches)

explanation.surface: Someone stands up straight just before being caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman dismissed by a fielder catching the ball is 'caught'; scorecards shorten this to Ct.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that appears upright is standing vertically, the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: 'Dead? Not us!' — becoming disturbed and alarmed

indicators.note: the letters of the quoted words are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: People insisting they are not dead grow agitated and frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astonished and shocked by something overlaps closely with being alarmed by it.

clue.text: Drunken males getting stuck into my wine

indicators.note: one piece is lodged inside the other, as the jumbled males go inside my
drunken suggests the letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: Tipsy men are tucking into the speaker's wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmsey is a sweet fortified Madeira, a type of the general term.

clue.text: Stick unusually hard with twice initial efficiency

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are arranged in an unusual order
the selected letter is used two times over
initial picks the opening letter of the word efficiency

explanation.surface: A recipe for sticking hard, done with double the usual efficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice initial efficiency' gives EE, which joins HARD before 'unusually' rearranges all six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling or bond to it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bill, joining Edward, performed on stage

indicators.note: the second piece joins on after the first

parts.note: a bill passed by Parliament becomes an act
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Bill and Edward teamed up and put on a show together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name beside Edward, but it is a parliamentary bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform a role in a play is what an actor does; the past tense matches.

clue.text: It may be cast in two ways, so he or she may make it

definitions.text: It may be cast in two ways

indicators.note: the five little words can be rearranged to make the item

explanation.surface: A riddle about something cast two ways, which either a man or a woman could produce.
explanation.walkthrough: The object is cast in metal by a smith, and a horse casts (throws) it when it comes loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrier's iron shoe is both cast in a foundry and cast off by the horse, two senses of the verb.

clue.text: Well-founded desert isle with lake

indicators.note: the last piece is placed alongside the others

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
Iona is a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A deserted island with a lake, described as solidly based.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' reads as a noun with the isle but is the verb to rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-founded view rests on sound reasoning, which is what a logical, sensible one does.

clue.text: Concede mixing up East with South and North at intervals

indicators.note: mixing up tells us to shuffle the letters
the two compass letters are spread out among the others rather than kept together

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A navigator admits confusing east with south, while north keeps appearing now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede a point is to agree to it, so the verb for giving agreement fits.

clue.text: Articulate fib about arranged treat

indicators.note: the lie goes about, around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: a fib is a lie

indicators.note: arranged indicates the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A well-spoken person tells a fib about a treat that was set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like a verb at the start, but it is the adjective defining the answer; 'arranged' scrambles TREAT into TERAT before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulate person expresses themself well, as an educated, well-read writer does.

clue.text: Those performing for pleasure are a must to broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast in its sense of scattered widely says the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Hobbyist performers are essential for a radio or TV broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-professionals perform for the love of it rather than pay, the root sense of the word.

clue.text: Moaned about guardian spirit

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complained about their guardian angel.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek belief a daemon was an attendant or inner spirit watching over a person.

clue.text: Pelt the principal of the school you attend? Show some shame!

parts.note: a pelt is an animal skin, or hide

parts.words: the principal of the school you attend
parts.note: the person running your school is your head teacher

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw things at your headteacher, followed by a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb, to throw at, but is the noun for an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be thoroughly ashamed, as if wanting to cover your face from view.

clue.text: Courage perceived to be genuine

parts.note: heart means courage, as in take heart
felt means sensed or perceived

explanation.surface: The bravery that was noticed turns out to be real.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere, deeply felt emotions are genuine rather than put on.

clue.text: Sum a union distributed as agreed

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: A sum of money shared out by a trade union, as everyone agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision everyone shares is fully agreed, with nobody dissenting.

clue.text: It may produce winter ailments leading to little sleep

definitions.text: It may produce winter ailments leading to little sleep

indicators.note: the first piece leads, coming before the second

parts.note: colds are the common illnesses of winter
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A spell of bitter weather brings on sniffles and keeps people awake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spell of freezing weather is the classic cause of seasonal chills and sniffles.

clue.text: Two things a fiddler may do to appear excessively deferential

definitions.text: Two things a fiddler may do
definitions.meaning: a violinist draws the ... the strings
the idiom means to behave in a fawning, obsequious way

explanation.surface: A violinist's actions doubling as a picture of grovelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from bowing low with a backward scrape of the foot, an obsequious greeting.

clue.text: Cannot even contract for an eating place

parts.note: cannot contracts to can't
even contracted is the poetic e'en

explanation.surface: Someone unable even to sign a contract for a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' works on both words: cannot shortens to CAN'T and even to E'EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria at a workplace or school, a kind of dining room.

clue.text: Silver's hiding part of face in pain

indicators.note: the outer piece hides the inner one within it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver; the 's stands for has
the chin is a part of the face

explanation.surface: Long John Silver covering up a sore part of his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sore and throbbing is to be in pain; the participle works as an adjective.

clue.text: One whose leader goes out every morning

definitions.text: One whose leader goes out every morning

parts.words: One whose leader goes out every morning
parts.note: a newspaper's leader is its daily opinion piece, and the person in charge of the paper sends it out each morning

explanation.definitionFit: The head of a daily newspaper writes or signs off the leading article that appears each morning.

clue.text: With lots of space, tie a ship up by end of day

indicators.note: by puts the last piece beside the first
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to moor is to tie a ship up

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Mooring a ship at the end of the day where there is plenty of room.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious is the plain sense: a room with plenty of space inside it.

clue.text: Trouble is found in small change perhaps

indicators.note: found in puts the word is inside the other piece

parts.note: a nuance is a slight difference or shade, a small change

explanation.surface: The trouble is all in the loose coins in your pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' suggests coins, but here it is a subtle variation; 'perhaps' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoyance or bother, a noun synonym of trouble.

clue.text: Bit of speech the actor didn't rehearse

definitions.text: Bit of speech the actor didn't rehearse

parts.words: Bit of speech the actor didn't rehearse
parts.note: an improvised line made up on the spot, not from the script

explanation.definitionFit: An improvised remark spoken without preparation is a classic piece of unscripted theatre.

clue.text: One usually gets into a flap at its opening time

definitions.text: One usually gets into a flap at its opening time

parts.words: One usually gets into a flap at its opening time
parts.note: a letter holder is entered via its flap, which is lifted when it is opened

explanation.definitionFit: Postal covers have a gummed flap that you get into when opening them.

clue.text: Boring plant

parts.note: plant means industrial installation and boring means drilling, not dull

explanation.definitionFit: An offshore drilling installation bores into the seabed for petroleum.

clue.text: One is not keen to show it

definitions.text: One is not keen to show it

parts.words: One is not keen to show it
parts.note: someone lacking enthusiasm displays indifference

explanation.definitionFit: Lack of interest or enthusiasm is shown by someone who is not keen on anything.

clue.text: More than one beastly food container — that depends!

definitions.text: More than one beastly food container — that depends!

parts.words: More than one beastly food container — that depends!
parts.note: feed bags for horses hang, or depend, from the animal's head

explanation.definitionFit: Feed bags are hung over a horse's muzzle, so they literally depend, or hang down.
